query: The cell cycle in somatic cells consists of four phases: (1) in G1 phase a cell grows and prepares for DNA replication; (2) in S phase the DNA is replicated; (3) in G2 phase a cell prepares for segregation of the replicated genome; (4) in M phase (or mitosis) the cell divides and can then either enter into G1 phase of the next cell cycle or it can (temporarily) exit the cell cycle and enter into G0 phase (i.e. quiescence).
